primary_source.citation: Itai Benjamini and Oded Schramm, Percolation Beyond Z^d, Many Questions and a Few Answers, Electronic Communications in Probability 1 (1996), 71-82, Conjecture 4 and Section 2
primary_source.quote_conjecture: Conjecture 4 Critical percolation dies in every almost transitive graph (assuming pc < 1).
primary_source.quote_model: Throughout the paper, site percolation is discussed. Except when dealing with planar graphs, the results and questions remain equally valid, with only minor modifications, for bond percolation.
primary_source.quote_graph_scope: The graphs we shall consider will always be locally finite
primary_source.quote_connected: We assume throughout that the graph G is connected.

exact_statement: For every infinite, connected, locally finite graph G with finitely many vertex orbits under Aut(G) and Bernoulli site percolation critical parameter p_c(G)<1, at p=p_c(G) there is almost surely no infinite open cluster. The bond-percolation analogue is explicitly indicated by the authors and stated as Conjecture 1.1 in Hutchcroft (2016).

bond_source.citation: Tom Hutchcroft, Critical percolation on any quasi-transitive graph of exponential growth has no infinite clusters, Comptes Rendus Mathematique 354 (2016), 944-947, Conjecture 1.1 and Theorem 1.2
bond_source.quote_conjecture: Let G be a quasi-transitive graph. If pc(G) < 1, then G[pc] has no infinite clusters almost surely.
bond_source.scope: Independent Bernoulli bond percolation on connected, locally finite graphs; the exponential-growth case is proved as Theorem 1.2.
